summary: Executed full backend (25 pytest tests, 100% pass) + frontend Playwright tests of Carta dei Vini. All critical flows pass: login (incl. wrong-pass error, unauth 401), wine CRUD with comma-decimal prices (24,50 / 25,00), gallery+list views, search, filters/reset, favorite toggle, detail dialog (shows prezzo in carta, acquisto, ricarico), Produttori page+filter link (/vini?produttore=X), Regioni e tipologie, Preferiti, Carta per i clienti (NO 'Prezzo di acquisto' label and no purchase price values displayed; both carta switches present), Account page (create-user-button), Backup page (export-csv, export-excel, download-backup buttons), mobile nav + more sheet. Backend verified: CSV export is UTF-8 BOM + semicolon + Italian headers, XLSX is a valid zip, backup JSON has wines+photos, restore is admin-only (403 for staff), invalid file -> 400, no public registration endpoint, GET /api/files requires auth (401). All TEST_ data created was deleted at the end; DB ends with 0 wines and only the seeded admin user.

issues: After submitting the wine form, the detail dialog auto-opens on top of the list. The underlying DialogOverlay sometimes lingers and intercepts pointer events on surrounding controls (e.g. view-mode toggle) until an Escape/close is issued. Not a blocker for real users (they click the X), but it is a minor UX+automation nit — consider closing the form dialog cleanly without immediately opening the detail dialog, or ensuring the overlay unmounts synchronously on close.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~500 lines and still coherent, but could be split into routers (auth, users, wines, export, backup) for maintainability.
login_attempts collection has no TTL index for cleanup; consider adding a TTL on created_at or expireAfter on locked_until to keep the collection small.
Access cookie expires in 15 min; frontend relies on silent /auth/refresh — ensure 401 interceptor handles refresh race on parallel requests.
backup/restore reads the whole payload (including base64 photos) into memory — fine for small catalogs but consider streaming / size cap for large restores.
